lines.label: PTAC exterior louver / architectural wall grille at the window wall
lines.where: Exterior face of the PTAC sleeve, visible from outside and through the unit's outdoor section
lines.src: M201 PTAC notes · M501 det.9 · M401 KN1 · A200 keyed note 8 (= AS105 kn 8) · AS103 PTAC detail · size ref 'A-601' (sheet not in the issued set — RFI R-04)
lines.instanceNote: FIVE STATEMENTS, NO RESOLUTION. (1) M201: 'POLYPROPYLENE LOUVER KIT (COLOR BY ARCHITECT)'. (2) M501 det.9: 'ALUMINUM ARCHITECTURAL-STYLE GRILLE FACTORY-PAINTED TO MATCH EXTERIOR WALL'. (3) M401 KN1: 'furnished with unit; painted to match exterior wall'. (4) A200 kn 8: 'INTEGRAL ALUMINUM LOUVER AT PTAC UNITS' — part of the WINDOW system, i.e. glazing sub, not a PTAC accessory. (5) AS103: 'integral louver to be installed with window system'. Disagreement spans MATERIAL (polypropylene vs aluminium), FINISH METHOD, and SCOPE (HVAC sub vs glazing sub). Polypropylene is moulded in colour and generally cannot be field-painted, so M201's product and M401's paint instruction may be physically incompatible. Compounding: the size reference points at sheet A-601, which does not exist in the issued set (set has A600 Doors, A610 Windows). SETTLES IT: one RFI to MWT / the M-EOR covering material, finish, colour and which sub buys it, plus the A601→A610 correction.
lines.verifyAtPunch: From outside: louver present, straight, seated, fastened, blades undamaged, sealant continuous; RECORD the material actually installed (plastic vs aluminium) and compare against the approved submittal before writing anything up.

lines.label: Interior architectural wall grille at the PTAC, painted to match the INTERIOR wall (M401 KN5)

lines.src: M401 KN5 ('grille painted to match INTERIOR wall') against M401 KN1 (same wording, 'EXTERIOR wall')

M401 prints two nearly identical keyed notes, KN1 (exterior face) and KN5 (interior face), and does NOT say whether that is ONE grille whose two faces are painted two different colours or TWO separate grilles. M401's body text reads it as one grille with two faces ('painted to match exterior wall (exterior face) and interior wall (interior face)'); M401's own implications line reads it as 'exterior + interior wall grilles' — plural. It decides whether there is a separate painted grille inside the finished room to inspect, and whose paint scope the room-side face is. Qty 1 is not stated — it is the reading if a second grille exists. SETTLES IT: same RFI as the exterior louver — ask the M-EOR whether KN1 and KN5 describe one grille or two, and who paints the interior face and to which PT code.
lines.verifyAtPunch: Look at the room-side face of the PTAC/sleeve — if a separate grille is there, confirm it is fastened, undamaged and painted to the adjacent wall colour (not mill/white); if there is NO separate interior grille, record that, because that is the evidence that closes the flag.

lines.label: Aldes constant-airflow regulator at the 50 CFM ceiling exhaust inlet
lines.where: Immediately behind/above the EAG-50 grille at the toilet exhaust inlet
lines.src: M305 exhaust-riser diagrams EV-1…EV-7 ('CEILING GRILLE EXHAUST 50 CFM c/w ALDES CONSTANT AIRFLOW REGULATOR' at each inlet) — the ONLY source
lines.instanceNote: The item is real and named verbatim at every inlet M305 draws. What is NOT established is that there is one in every guestroom, because the only sheet that scopes them does not add up: M305's seven riser totals sum to 2,450 CFM = exactly 49 inlets at 50 CFM, against roughly 119 needed (115 keys + 4 ice-machine alcoves) — 41% coverage. Independently, three of the four roof fans are scheduled BELOW the riser CFM assigned to them (EF-8 200 vs 350; EF-9 300-350 vs 650; EF-11 400-450 vs 850; only EF-10/EV-6 balances), an 850 CFM aggregate shortfall. Qty 1 is M305's per-inlet drawing, NOT a verified per-room count. Do not price 115 and do not price 49. SETTLES IT: the M-EOR reconciling the EV riser schedule against the room count and the roof-fan capacities — and 16 presence/absence data points off this walk is real evidence for that RFI.
lines.verifyAtPunch: Drop the EAG-50 grille and look — is a constant-airflow regulator installed behind it, YES or NO? Record per room; if absent, log it, do NOT write it as a deficiency until the EOR answers.

A grille-only inlet and a dedicated in-room fan cannot both be true. Supporting but not conclusive: E400's Panel A and Panel B guestroom schedules carry NO exhaust-fan circuit — though remark 3 would put a fan on the Lighting circuit needing no dedicated breaker. coordination_issues C-06, a 115-unit buy. Do not order 115 Panasonic FV-0511VK2 on this. SETTLES IT faster than any RFI: look behind one bath grille on this walk.

(2) LOCATION: M401 says bath; A555 places keynote 20 on a bed/sofa-wall elevation, which is not the bath wall; A550's transcription does not name which elevation carries it. Also relevant: M301 GN13 permits a lined transfer duct OR a door undercut where make-up air is under 50 CFM (M101 legend defines UC at 1/2"), but no sheet places an undercut at a guestroom bath door, so none is claimed here. lines.label: Access panel in the bath ceiling to the fire damper and volume damper — min 12"x12", with the permanent damper label
lines.where: Would be in the 7'-3" PT-07 painted-gypsum bath lid, at the FD/VD above it
lines.src: M101 GN7 (min 12"x12" access to dampers) · M301 Key Note 4 · M501 (fire/smoke damper access + permanent exterior label) · M101 GN31/GN32 — AGAINST A550 view 02, which draws no access panel
lines.instanceNote: DB GAP, and it is the most transferable finding on the walk. The requirement is PRINTED — M101 GN7 requires min 12"x12" access to dampers, M301 KN4 requires an access panel above the ceiling for HVAC maintenance, and M501 requires fire/smoke dampers to have approved access with a permanent exterior label in letters at least 1/2" high — but the placement is MISSING: none of the ten A550–A556 guestroom RCPs draws one, and the only flush-access-panel keynote in the whole A12x/A55x set (A121 kn 5) is at the ICE-MACHINE alcove, not a guestroom. Every floor-1 bath has a hard painted-gyp lid at 7'-3" with the Ruskin CFD4 fire damper and the VD above it. Qty is not stated by any sheet — 1 is the minimum the notes imply. This is a real, repeating 115-room omission, an RFI candidate and a CO-inspection exposure, since an inspector cannot verify a damper he cannot reach. Not invented — only the placement is missing. SETTLES IT: RFI to the M-EOR / MWT asking where the guestroom bath damper access panel goes and who provides it.
lines.verifyAtPunch: Look at the bath ceiling — is there an access panel, YES or NO? If yes: min 12"x12", flush, latching, painted, and carrying the permanent FIRE DAMPER label in letters at least 1/2" high. If no: photograph the intact lid. Cut nothing.

ROOM 104 IS ONE OF SIX CANDIDATES FOR THE FLOOR-1 HEARING-IMPAIRED KEY, AND THE REGISTER DOES NOT EXIST. A100's Guestroom Matrix floor-1 King column prints 'King Studio — 5 S' and 'King Studio, HI — 1 T', while room_map and the DB carry SIX plain King Studios on floor 1 (104, 106, 108, 110, 112, 114). 5 + 1 = 6, so exactly one of those six is the communication-features key. A100's own first-floor plan HAS NEVER BEEN SCANNED for the E500-defined 'INDICATES HEARING IMPAIRED SUITE' symbol, and A100 is not even named in coordination_issues C-04's action list. This decides 3 strobes and a doorbell on 104. ACTION BEFORE THE WALK, NOT DURING: read A100 at full scale for the crossed-ear symbol across the 16 first-floor rooms and cross-check E501 / the FA-2 first-floor room regions. Cheapest open item on the sheet. Mobility is NOT hearing — 118 being the accessible key proves nothing here.

NEW FINDING — A100'S FLOOR-1 KING SUB-TOTAL CONTRADICTS ITS OWN ROWS, AND FLOOR 1 IS THE ONLY FLOOR WHERE IT DOES. A100's floor-1 King rows are: King Studio 5 S · King Studio CD 1 T · King Studio HI 1 T · King Studio ACC MOD CD 1 T = 8 rooms, 3 tubs / 5 showers. But A100's own 'King Sub-Total (T / S)' row prints 0 / 8 for floor 1 — zero tubs. Floors 2 (1/18), 3 (1/18) and 4 (2/18) each reconcile EXACTLY to their rows; only floor 1 fails. Consequences: (a) it weakens the otherwise attractive field lead that the floor-1 HI King Studio can be found by looking for the one with a tub — do not lean on it; (b) it puts a question mark on room 104's bathing fixture, which is why the SH-1/SH-4 shower line is graded MEDIUM rather than the DB's HIGH; (c) it feeds coordination_issues C-01 (tub vs roll-in on the accessible keys). Raise with MWT CA alongside the existing C-01 / A11 RFI.

TWENTY-FOUR OF THE 77 MEP ROWS ON 104 ARE CONCEALED ROUGH-IN AND WERE NOT EMITTED AS PUNCH LINES. ELECTRICAL (13): ITM-0002 feeder · ITM-0003 lighting circuit · ITM-0004 convenience-receptacle circuit · ITM-0005 bathroom GFCI circuit · ITM-0006 refrigerator 173 VA · ITM-0007 disposer 480 VA · ITM-0008 dishwasher 1068 VA · ITM-0009 microwave/hood 850 VA · ITM-0010 PTAC 208 V 2080 VA · ITM-0011 and ITM-0012 small appliance 1500 VA each · ITM-0013 spare breaker · ITM-0018 thermostat power/control wiring rough-in. Their punch-visible ends are folded into the PNL "A" panelboard line (every breaker present, labelled, AFCI/GFCI test buttons trip, one spare) and into the device lines at the other end. PLUMBING (7): ITM-0035 domestic water branch set · ITM-0036 fixture runouts · ITM-0037 sanitary riser tie · ITM-0038 vent riser · ITM-0039 WC waste · ITM-0040 2" SS waste branch · ITM-0041 vent piping — all in-wall/below-slab, tested indirectly at the fixtures, which are all on the sheet. MECHANICAL (4): ITM-0062 4" fresh-air duct above ceiling · ITM-0063 4" toilet exhaust duct to the EV riser · ITM-0068 fire-caulk at rated duct penetrations (explicitly on Austin's OUT list) · ITM-0061 in part, see the next problem.

ITM-0061 MIXES CONCEALED ROUGH-IN WITH FINISHED WORK IN ONE ROW AND SHOULD BE SPLIT IN THE DB. It reads 'PTAC field-built sub-base; PTAC edge above carpet tiles; stone stool set over the unit.' The FIELD-BUILT SUB-BASE (M501 det.9, 'field-built sub-base — see arch') is named explicitly on Austin's OUT list and is buried under the PTAC and behind the drywall closure by the time the room is finished — dropped. THE DB ASSERTS A CONTESTED READING AS FACT ON ALL THREE SPRINKLER ROWS. ITM-0156/0157/0158 describe the heads as 'Concealed pendent sprinkler head on drop' at reliability HIGH. FP-1's description column prints only 'VK430 7/16 FR 155 C PD' — 'concealed pendent' is packages/fire-appliance.md's READING of the 'PD' suffix, not a printed word. Against it, A120/A121/A122/A123 General Note I reads verbatim: 'SPRINKLER HEADS IN CEILINGS IN PUBLIC AREAS TO BE CONCEALED. ALL OTHER HEADS TO BE SEMI-RECESSED.' A guest room is not a public area, so that note requires SEMI-RECESSED in 104. Concealed = flush cover plate; semi-recessed = escutcheon with a visible deflector — two different looks from the floor and two different buys (concept-page conflict FS-3, which notes 437 VK430 building-wide is far more than the public areas can absorb). Lines re-labelled to the verbatim FP-1 string and downgraded to MEDIUM. Two further items nothing in the set states: no cover-plate or escutcheon FINISH or COLOUR appears on any sheet, and FP-1 has NO temperature column — the '155' sits inside the model string and the 'C' is not decoded anywhere — so neither may go on a purchase document off this row. HEAD COUNT ITSELF IS SOUND for 104: room 108, a King Studio, was read head-by-head at 700–800 dpi and shows 3.

INTERIOR ARCHITECTURAL WALL GRILLE AT THE PTAC (M401 KN5) IS MISSING FROM THE DB. M401 prints two nearly identical keyed notes — KN1 'painted to match exterior wall' and KN5 'painted to match interior wall' — and does not say whether that is one grille with two painted faces or two separate grilles. M401's body text (drawings/M401.md line 25) reads it as one grille, 'painted to match exterior wall (exterior face) and interior wall (interior face)'; M401's own implications line (line 47) reads it as 'exterior + interior wall grilles', plural. If a second grille exists it is squarely visible in the finished room and carries a paint scope. Emitted sheets-only, FLAGGED.

ACCESS PANEL TO THE BATH FIRE DAMPER AND VOLUME DAMPER IS MISSING FROM THE DB, AND IT IS A 115-ROOM OMISSION WITH CO EXPOSURE. M101 GN7 requires min 12"x12" access to dampers, M301 Key Note 4 requires an access panel above the ceiling for HVAC maintenance, and M501 requires fire/smoke dampers to have approved access with a permanent exterior label in letters at least 1/2" high — but NONE of the ten A550–A556 guestroom RCPs draws one, and the only flush-access-panel keynote in the whole A12x/A55x set (A121 kn 5) is at the ice-machine alcove. Every floor-1 bath has a hard 7'-3" PT-07 gyp lid with the Ruskin CFD4 and the VD above it. The requirement is printed; only the placement is missing. An inspector cannot verify a damper he cannot reach. RFI to the M-EOR / MWT; this walk supplies the 16-room evidence.

DISHWASHER DISCONNECT SWITCH (E101 GENERAL NOTE #4, verbatim 'Dishwasher switches in cabinet under sink.') IS MISSING FROM THE DB. The dedicated dishwasher CIRCUIT is well supported (E400 Panel A, E103 1068 VA, kn10 placed on A550 view 04) but the SWITCH is a set-wide general note with no guestroom placement — no guestroom sheet places a keynote or symbol for it — and the kitchenette sink it would sit under is itself unresolved. Emitted sheets-only, FLAGGED. Do not write it up as missing until the EC confirms whether GN#4 was carried into the guestrooms.

THREE FURTHER SHEETS-ONLY GAPS EMITTED. (1) WIRING DEVICES AND COVER PLATES GENERALLY — nothing in the DB catches plate colour/series consistency, which is the classic guestroom punch item; and the ONLY device colour printed anywhere in the set is WHITE, at the microwave outlet (kn36), with E101 #14 saying only 'coordinated with architect' and GN#2 'clarify brand with franchise/owner before ordering'. There is nothing to punch a colour against until Triun produces the approved wiring-device submittal. (2) CONNECTED ROOM EDGE CONTROLLER — named twice in kn47 and once in E101 GN#8 and nowhere else in the set: no mark, no symbol, no schedule, no count, no location. (3) GUESTROOM ENTRY CARD LOCK (A600 HW Set #1 'Advance Card Lock') — the only lock or access device the set draws in a guest room; no security/CCTV/access-control design exists anywhere (gap LV-5). NEEDS AUSTIN'S RULING on whether the card lock punches here or on the doors/hardware sheet, since the DB already carries door GR-1 under 'Doors' — decide once so it is neither double-punched nor missed.

TWO ZERO-QUANTITY CONFIRM ROWS EMITTED, BOTH NEEDING AUSTIN'S RULING ON WHETHER HE WANTS THEM ON THE SHEET AT ALL. (1) NO SPRINKLER HEAD IN THE GUEST BATH — an OBSERVATION on rooms 107 and 108 only, not a ruling; write 'no head drawn', never 'no head required', because the governing standard is itself open (conflicts.md B5.3: FP-1 designs to NFPA 13-2021, G100 checks NFPA 13-07 with 13R unchecked AND both 'Partial' and 'Yes' ticked, G002 note 8 says NFPA 13 flat, project context says 13R). (2) NO CO DETECTOR IN THE GUEST ROOM — this is an ABSENCE, not a verified exclusion: no sheet states guest rooms are exempt, it simply never places one, and FA-1 schedules only 3 SKFIRECOW units for the whole gas-fired 115-key building (fire-alarm conflict FA-8). Both rows exist so the walker neither false-flags an absence nor walks past something not on the drawings.

SCOPE DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO EXTRACTORS ON THE BATH FIRE DAMPER (FD, Ruskin CFD4) — RESOLVED IN FAVOUR OF 'IN' PER AUSTIN'S ARGUABLE-CALL RULE, AND FLAGGED FOR HIS RULING. The mechanical package excludes it as rough-in (body above a 7'-3" hard lid with no access panel drawn — matches Austin's own OUT example of a damper with no access). The fire package carries it IN (checked at a visible point, the EAG-50 grille, and the drawings themselves require accessible, labelled access per M101 GN7 and GN31/GN32). Emitted IN, FLAGGED, and moved from the DB's 'Mechanical' category to 'Fire Protection' so it does not fall through the gap between the two trade lists — the move is stated on the line, not silent. Related trap carried on the line: E500 FA Note 7 says all fire dampers connect to an FA relay and close on general alarm, but M501 det.2 shows the CFD4 as a FUSIBLE-LINK damper with no actuator (the motorised type on this job is det.5, used elsewhere), so a walker will not find a wire there and must not write it up as missing.

THE NOT-APPROVED LAVATORY SUBSTITUTION ROW (ITM-0045) WAS NOT EMITTED AS A STANDALONE PUNCH LINE — IT IS FOLDED INTO THE LAVATORY FAUCET LINE AS A REJECTION TEST, AND THIS IS THE NOTICE SO IT IS NOT SILENTLY DROPPED. The S4 product data offers three American Standard Studio bowl models with none ticked and two Moen M·Dura faucets with neither ticked, no transmittal and no stamp — under the precedence chain that is not a submittal and supersedes nothing, so the fixtures of record stay P104's Decolav Callensia 1402-CWH + Delta 581LF-GPM-PP. A zero-quantity 'NOT APPROVED' row reads as noise on a crew punch sheet; the check a walker actually performs is COUNT THE DECK HOLES (3 = approved Delta, 1 = the unapproved Moen), which now sits on the faucet line. If the substitution is ever stamped it changes the countertop cutout from 3-hole to 1-hole on 115 vanity tops (OPEN_ITEMS A3).

NO PER-ROOM DEVICE COUNTS EXIST ANYWHERE IN THIS SOURCE SET, AND THE DB CARRIES NONE — SEVEN LINES ARE THEREFORE EMITTED AT qty 1 AS PLACEHOLDERS WITH FLAGGED OR MEDIUM: convenience receptacles, data outlets, extended J-boxes (kn25), entry/closet/general lighting, S21 bath downlight, WS03 vanity sconce, telephone. E400 and A550 view 04 are the only device layouts and their counts live on the source PDFs — the device symbols are GRAPHICS, not text, so text extraction will keep returning nothing (packages/electrical.md open item 14, 'no takeoff attempted'; low-voltage gap LV-3). What IS printed and usable is the A550 view-04 device-spacing dimension string: bed wall 8'-1", 2'-1 1/2", 7'-2", 3'-0"; working wall 6'-5", 4'-0", 6", 3'-5 1/2", 8 1/2", 1'-3", 9 1/2", 2'-9 1/2", 10", 1'-4", 1'-0", 6", 2'-4", 1'-0". ACTION BEFORE THE WALK: pull the counts off the E400 and A550 PDFs at full scale, or walk 104 with the low-voltage integrator and set the baseline there — otherwise the walker has nothing to check against on seven lines.

MOUNTING HEIGHTS ARE NOT SETTLED AND THIS IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST WRITE-UP HAZARD ON THE WALK — INSTRUCT THE WALKER TO RECORD, NOT JUDGE. RECEPTACLE / DATA / TV / TELEPHONE: 12" AFF (A530 GENERAL NOTES note D, verbatim 'A.F.F. WALL RECEPTACLES/DATA PORTS TO [B]E MOUNTED @ 12" TYPICAL U.N.O', byte-identical on A531, A532, A532.1 and A533 — five bath sheets) vs 18" AFF (E101 spec #18, E101 symbol legend, G400 detail 02 'ALL RECEPTACLES SHALL BE 18" A.F.F. UNLESS NOTED OTHERWISE'). THERMOSTAT: 48" (A550 kn24 max-to-top, M101 GN29, G402 note 11, G400) vs 54" non-accessible (M401 KN4, the only source for it) vs 60" (E101 legend). SWITCH: 46" (G400 det.02) vs 48" (E101 legend; kn3 as a MAX at the bath) vs 54" (E101 spec #18). G402 note 11 caps all guest controls at 15"–48". coordination_issues C-03 / packages/electrical.md open item 1 — OPEN RFI. The one height that IS a stated hard MAX and can be enforced today is kn3's 48" to the top of the bathroom switch.

PTAC EXTERIOR LOUVER — FIVE STATEMENTS, NO RESOLUTION, SPANNING MATERIAL, FINISH METHOD AND WHICH SUB BUYS IT. (1) M201: 'polypropylene louver kit (color by architect)'. (2) M501 det.9: 'aluminum architectural-style grille factory-painted to match exterior wall'. (3) M401 KN1: 'furnished with unit; painted to match exterior wall'. (4) A200 keyed note 8: 'ALUMINUM FIXED WINDOW ... WITH INTEGRAL ALUMINUM LOUVER AT PTAC UNITS' — part of the WINDOW system, i.e. the glazing sub's buy, not a PTAC accessory. (5) AS103: 'integral louver to be installed with window system'. Polypropylene is moulded in colour and generally cannot be field-painted to an architect's colour, so M201's product and M401's paint instruction may be physically incompatible. Compounding: A200/AS105 cite sheet A-601 for louver SIZES and A-601 IS NOT IN THE ISSUED SET (the set has A600 Doors and A610 Windows; eighteen sheets point at A601) — RFI R-04 — so the louver has no dimensional source either. One RFI to MWT / the M-EOR should cover material, finish, colour, buying sub and the A601→A610 correction. Also confirm whether M301 Key Note 3 (corrosion-resistant ≥1/4" mesh insect screen on louvers) extends to the PTAC louver; that note is written in the combustion-air context and does not name the PTAC.

EF-1 — AN IN-ROOM BATH FAN OR A DESIGNATION FOR A GRILLE INLET? A 115-UNIT BUY, UNRESOLVED (coordination_issues C-06). M201 schedules EF-1 as a real Panasonic FV-0511VK2 ceiling fan, 50 CFM, with remark 3 'switch w/ room lights', remark 5 backdraft damper and remark 6 off-white aluminium grille, and M202/M301–M304 all repeat it as the guest-toilet exhaust. But M305's riser diagrams show every guestroom inlet as a PLAIN CEILING GRILLE + Aldes constant-airflow regulator on a central riser driven by roof fans EF-8…EF-11, with no in-room fan anywhere. Mutually exclusive. E400's Panel A and Panel B guestroom schedules carry NO exhaust-fan circuit, which leans grille-only but is not conclusive because remark 3 would put a fan on the Lighting circuit needing no dedicated breaker. DO NOT ORDER 115 PANASONIC FV-0511VK2. Closable on this walk faster than by RFI: look behind one bath ceiling grille in 104 and record fan housing vs bare duct.

ALDES CONSTANT-AIRFLOW REGULATOR COUNT IS NOT SUPPORTED BY ITS ONLY SOURCE — the single most expensive unverified line in the mechanical package. M305 is the only sheet that scopes them and it does not add up: its seven riser totals sum to 2,450 CFM, which at 50 CFM per inlet is exactly 49 inlets, against roughly 119 needed (115 guestrooms + 4 ice-machine alcoves) — 41% coverage. Independently, three of the four roof fans are scheduled BELOW the riser CFM assigned to them (EF-8 200 vs EV-1+EV-3 350; EF-9 300–350 vs EV-4+EV-5 650; EF-11 400–450 vs EV-2+EV-7 850; only EF-10/EV-6 balances at 600) — an 850 CFM aggregate shortfall. Either the seven risers drawn are a partial set or the riser CFM totals are wrong, and M305 does not say which. Separately, which EV riser serves which floor-1 room is not determinable: M301 shows only EV-1, EV-2, EV-5 and EV-6 reaching floor 1, yet M305 draws all seven spanning Attic/4th/3rd/2nd/1st. Do not price 115 and do not price 49. Recording presence/absence behind the grille in all 16 rooms is real evidence for the RFI.

GUESTROOM FLOOR DRAIN — TWO SHEETS DISAGREE ON WHETHER 104 GETS ONE, AND THE ITEM HAS NO MARK AND NO SCHEDULED PRODUCT. P402 places the floor drain in ACCESSIBLE UNITS; A530 keyed note 20 places one on the STANDARD guest-bath plan 01, which is the plan governing room 104 (A530's title block covers King Std., Std. Conn., QQ Std., Std. Conn., QQ Wide and QQ Ext.). Both readings carried, neither resolved. Separately, P104's Drain and Drainage Appurtenance Schedule carries FD-1 (Mechanical/Laundry, Zurn Z550), FD-2 (Unfinished Spaces, Zurn Z415B) and FD-3 (Funnel, Zurn Z514E) — none is a guestroom drain — so no make, model or strainer finish is specified for the item the walker is standing over. The same open question carries the trap guard/primer line with it, which itself has two scheduled products (P102 Sioux Chief 695 vs P104 TP-1 PPP SMP-500-115V) and neither scoped to a guest bath. Recording present/absent in all 16 baths answers half of it by itself.

FIXTURE-MARK DRIFT — CARRY BOTH MARK SETS, PICK NO WINNER (conflicts.md B3.1, OPEN). This costs money, not semantics. The enlarged unit plans P401/P402 mark the guestroom shower SH-1 and the guestroom lavatory L-2; P104 schedules them SH-3/SH-4 and L-3/L-4. P104's OWN SH-1 is the 36"x36" EMPLOYEE shower (Kohler Sonata K-1689-0) and its OWN L-2 is the EMPLOYEE/POOL wall-hung lav (Decolav Lilac 1819W-1P-CWH with a battery Delta faucet) — order guestroom trim off the plan marks and the wrong pan and the wrong lavatory arrive. Two further unassigned items on the same sheets: WC-3 vs WC-4 is NEVER assigned per unit type (both marks print together on P401/P402; P104's descriptions imply ADA=WC-3 Champion Pro and standard=WC-4 Cadet Pro but no sheet states it), and NO SHEET IN THE SET STATES A GUESTROOM WATER-CLOSET SEAT HEIGHT, so no seat-height dimension may go on the punch sheet. Also unreconciled: A530 dimensions the shower compartment 5'-0" CLEAR x 3'-7 1/4" while P104 schedules a 30"x60" pan — 60" matches the 5'-0" but 30" does not match 3'-7 1/4", and neither sheet reconciles them.

SK-3 / SK-4 KITCHENETTE SINK — PLACEMENT GENUINELY UNKNOWN AND ALL-OR-NOTHING FOR FLOOR 1. P401 verbatim: 'a kitchenette/wet-bar sink (SK-3 / SK-4) in the suite/extended units'; P402 repeats it; neither assigns it to any of their seven unit plans, and P104 schedules NO product for either mark (a hole in the schedule, not mark drift). Floor 1 has no King One Bedroom suites and no QQ Extended rooms, so a literal reading gives ZERO kitchenette sinks on floor 1 including 104, while the 'every Home2 key is a suite' reading gives all 16. P201 riser #P2 does carry an SK on a guestroom stack (2" waste / 1-1/4" vent), proving one exists somewhere. Compounding: A550 tags 901 REFRIGERATOR and 902 DISHWASHER on the working wall and tags NO SINK — a dishwasher with no drawn sink is itself an RFI — and the S4 file titled 'Moen Kitchenette Faucet' is Moen 8227, whose own product sheet titles it 'Two-Handle LAVATORY Faucet with Spout', 8" widespread, 3-hole, which will not drop into a single-hole kitchenette deck. An RFI to the MEP EOR is already open; do not raise a second. Recording present/absent in all 16 rooms is the field evidence that closes it.

GUESTROOM SHUT-OFF VALVE ACCESS NEEDS A RULING BEFORE THE WALK — THE ACCESS PANEL IS DRAWN IN A CEILING THAT DOES NOT EXIST IN A GUESTROOM. P502 detail 3 draws the CWS/HWS/HWR gate valves behind an 18"x18" ACCESS PANEL in a SUSPENDED CEILING, and NO guestroom ceiling in this set is suspended — A550's RCP reads painted gypsum PT-07 at 8'-3 3/8" (main room) and 7'-3" (bath and entry). The only suspended ceiling near these rooms on floor 1 is Guest Corridor 121 (A120: alternating 8'-2" ACT grid bays and 8'-0" painted-gyp bulkhead bands). No access-panel symbol or keyed note is drawn in ANY guestroom. The sheets that would settle it — A425 details 09 and 11, the typical shaft plans — CANNOT BE QUOTED: A425.md marks everything below its verified room-number list as unverified speculative text, verbatim 'Do not quote any of it'; re-extract A425 page 52 from the source PDF before relying on it. Meanwhile P101 note 9 requires the GC to furnish access panels, P101 note 15 requires domestic-water valves 'located accessibly', and M101 N7 requires min 12"x12" access to valves — so the design clearly intends them reachable. SEPARATE VALVE-TYPE CONFLICT, BOTH READINGS CARRIED: P401 and P502 draw a GATE valve, P101 GN15 specifies BALL valves or approved equal. The three DB rows (ITM-0032/0033/0034) were collapsed into one line at qty 3 because the walker opens one panel.

DOUBLE-PUNCH HAZARDS TO SETTLE BEFORE THE SHEETS GO OUT. (1) THERMOSTAT — carried ONCE, under Mechanical. The DB also has an electrical thermostat-wiring row (ITM-0018, dropped as rough-in) and the low-voltage extractor carries the thermostat-to-PTAC comms path; both are folded into the single Mechanical line. Trade split per M101 N28: United Electric furnishes, routes and installs the control WIRING; Iceberg furnishes, installs and terminates the thermostat. (2) VANITY SCONCE — E101 schedules WS03 (Arkansas 3550V) as a base-build ELECTRICAL fixture while the FF&E set schedules GR-203 'VANITY SCONE' [sic] on every bath sheet, and the DB carries GR-203 on 104 under FF&E - Lighting as well; almost certainly ONE physical fixture in two packages, so the FF&E punch and this one must not both write it up. (3) SHOWER GLASS DOOR — kn28/kn5 is GLASS SUB scope, listed under Plumbing only because the walker tests it on the same pass as the pan and valve; do not bill it to Larry's Plumbing. (4) PTAC CONDENSATE — plumbing scope (Larry's) per M401 KN2 and M501 det.9 but the PTAC is HVAC (Iceberg); M401 records this as 'a frequent interface gap' — expect it to be nobody's until it is named. (5) CARD LOCK — see the sheets-only gaps problem.

critic.summary:
This is a strong list and most of it survives audit. Every piece of sheet arithmetic I could independently re-run checked out exactly: M305's seven riser totals do sum to 2,450 CFM = 49 inlets (200+400+150+300+350+600+450), all three roof-fan shortfalls are real (EF-8 200 vs 350, EF-9 300-350 vs 650, EF-11 400-450 vs 850, EF-10/EV-6 balances at 600), A100's floor-1 King rows really are 5S+1T+1T+1T against a printed "0 / 8" sub-total while floors 2/3/4 reconcile exactly, kn50 really is absent from A550 view 04's placed-keynote list (3,10,14,15,16,24,25,28,36,43,44,45,46,47,51,4), FA-1's 121/121 really does reconcile to 115 keys + 6 second detectors, and the PTAC-1 call for the King Studio family is confirmed twice (M301 "PTAC-1 at all 16 first-floor guestrooms"; M401 detail 03 not among the PTAC-2 details). Model data on the PTAC, WS03, S21, WC, lav, faucet, shower and sprinkler lines is verbatim off M201/E101/P104/FP-1 with no invention. Room-type discipline is good: Panel A not B, one one-way viewer not two, kn21/kn14-HADG/SH-3 correctly excluded, no motorized shade — I found no accessible-room item wrongly kept.

It breaks on three things. (1) MISSING DEVICES — the walker's hand touches an entry light switch, a refrigerator receptacle and three hardwired wall sconces, and none of the three is on the sheet. E400 names "switching (entry, bath w/ integrated night light)" and A550's legend carries "SWITCH, 3 WAY, 4 WAY", yet the only switches punched are the bath switch and the disposal switch. E400 Panel A carries a dedicated Refrigerator circuit (E103, 173 VA) and A550 tags 901 on the working wall, yet only the microwave outlet got a device line. And Austin explicitly named "wall sconces" — the DB carries GR-202 ×2 and GR-204 on 104 (ITM-0117/0118/0119) and they are hardwired; GR-203/WS03 was pulled in with a double-punch warning while these three were dropped silently with no ruling. (2) TWO PLUMBING FIXTURES OVER-FLAGGED — the WC line says "WHICH MARK GOES WHERE IS NEVER ASSIGNED," but P104's own description column prints WC-3 "(Guestroom, Floor Outlet, ADA)" against WC-4 "(Guestroom, Floor Outlet)", and L-3 "(Guestrooms, Undermount, Rect, ADA)" against L-4 "(Guestrooms, Undermount, Rect)". That is an assignment, printed. The shower line used exactly that logic to land on SH-4; the WC and lav lines refuse to. And the lav mark is misquoted — P401 and P402 print "L-2 / L-3", not "L-2", which guts the "order off the plan mark and the wrong lavatory arrives" alarm. (3) THE HI RESEARCH IS INCOMPLETE — E103's guestroom load analysis carries "King Studio, HI, CD = 1" and "King Studio, HI = 6" as separate rows, which corroborates G001's split against A100's undivided 7. E103 is cited five times elsewhere on this same list for VA loads. If G001+E103 are right, the floor-1 communication-features key is 116 and 104 is not a candidate at all — which is the whole basis for the qty-3 strobe line and the doorbell line.

defects.problem: There is no punch line for the switch a walker throws when they open the door. The only switches on the list are the bath switch with night light (kn3) and the garbage-disposal switch ganged with a duplex (kn14). A550's own POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND carries "SWITCH, 3 WAY, 4 WAY" as a distinct symbol, which implies switching from two locations, and none of that is captured. defects.line: MISSING LINE — Electrical: refrigerator receptacle / appliance connection at the working wall
defects.problem: The list punches the microwave outlet as its own device line (kn36, HIGH) but folds the refrigerator entirely into the panelboard line as concealed rough-in (ITM-0006, "Refrigerator branch circuit, 173 VA"). The circuit is rough-in; the RECEPTACLE the 901 refrigerator plugs into is not. defects.line: MISSING LINES — hardwired wall sconces GR-202 (×2) and GR-204
defects.problem: Austin named "wall sconces" as an explicitly in-scope punch item. The list carries exactly one — WS03 at the bath vanity — and correctly warns it is double-carried as FF&E GR-203. It carries none of the other three hardwired sconces in the room. A550 view 01 tags GR-202 NIGHTSTAND SCONCE twice (both nightstands, centreline 4'-4" per elevation 07) and GR-204 SCONCE @ WALL HOOK once on the working wall; the app DB carries all three on room 104 at HIGH (ITM-0118, ITM-0119, ITM-0117). The boundary is already porous in the other direction (WS03/GR-203 is in, and the A600 card lock is in with an explicit request for a ruling), so dropping these three silently is inconsistent rather than principled.
defects.correction: Either add three Electrical/lighting lines — GR-202 nightstand sconce ×2 (bed wall, CL 4'-4" per A550 elev 07, blocking per kn32/kn33) and GR-204 sconce @ wall hook ×1 (working wall) — at MEDIUM, or add a single explicit exclusion line in the same form as the card lock line: "NEEDS AUSTIN'S RULING — GR-202 ×2 and GR-204 are hardwired wall sconces the DB carries on 104 under FF&E - Lighting; decide once whether they punch here or on the FF&E sheet so they are neither double-punched nor missed." Do not leave them off with no note. verifyAtPunch if carried: each sconce level and at the elevation-07 4'-4" centreline, operates from its switch or its own body switch, canopy tight to WC-01/PT-02 with no gap or exposed fastener, mounted on blocking not hollow gyp.

A550 elevation 07: "4'-4" (nightstand-sconce CL)". defects.line: Plumbing — WC-3 / WC-4, "Water closet, guestroom…", reliability FLAGGED, instanceNote "(1) WHICH MARK GOES WHERE IS NEVER ASSIGNED"
defects.problem: That is not true, and the same list proves it elsewhere. P104's description column assigns the marks in print: WC-3 is "Water Closet (Guestroom, Floor Outlet, ADA)" and WC-4 is "Water Closet (Guestroom, Floor Outlet)" — no ADA. Room 104 is a standard non-accessible key, which the list states repeatedly on the Panel A line and the kn14 line. So 104 takes WC-4, Cadet Pro 215CA.104, on the same reading the SH-1/SH-4 line already used to pick SH-4 over SH-3 ("SH-3 Shower (Guestroom, ADA)… no threshold" vs "SH-4 Shower (Guestroom)… 4" threshold"). Calling the shower settled and the water closet unassigned, off identical schedule syntax, is internally inconsistent, and it over-flags an item the walker can be given a straight answer on.
defects.correction: Re-grade to MEDIUM. Keep the dual mark string as printed but state the reading: "P104's description column assigns WC-3 to ADA guestrooms and WC-4 to standard guestrooms — 104 is standard, so the fixture of record is WC-4, American Standard Cadet Pro 215CA.104. Carried MEDIUM rather than HIGH only because P401/P402 print the pair 'WC-3 / WC-4' on the unit plans without assigning per unit type. This is the same reading applied to SH-4 on the shower line." Keep the seat-height warning verbatim — that one is correct, no sheet in the set states a guestroom WC seat height. verifyAtPunch unchanged, but change "RECORD the model installed" to "RECORD the model installed — 215CA.104 is expected; a 211AA.104 in a standard key is the finding."
defects.citation: P104 Plumbing Fixture Schedule, rows 23–24 verbatim: "WC-3 | Water Closet (Guestroom, Floor Outlet, ADA) | American Standard | Champion Pro 211AA.104" and "WC-4 | Water Closet (Guestroom, Floor Outlet) | American Standard | Cadet Pro 215CA.104". Compare P104 rows 33–34: "SH-3 | Shower (Guestroom, ADA)… no threshold" / "SH-4 | Shower (Guestroom)… 4" threshold" — the syntax the shower line already relied on.

defects.line: Plumbing — L-2 / L-3 / L-4, "Lavatory bowl…", instanceNote "P401/P402 print L-2 on the unit plans"
defects.problem: Two faults. First, a misquote of the governing sheet: P401 and P402 do NOT print "L-2" alone — both print the pair "L-2 / L-3". P401: "lavatory (L-2 / L-3)". P402: "L-2 / L-3 (lavatory)". Because L-3 is already on the unit plans, the line's alarm — "order off the plan mark and the WRONG LAVATORY ARRIVES" — is materially overstated; the correct guestroom mark is sitting right there next to the drifted one. Second, the same ADA/non-ADA assignment the WC line missed applies here: P104 prints L-3 as "Lavatory (Guestrooms, Undermount, Rect, ADA)" and L-4 as "Lavatory (Guestrooms, Undermount, Rect)", so 104 takes L-4. Third and smallest, the mark string "L-2 / L-3 / L-4" is a synthesized composite that appears on no sheet, which is exactly what Austin's verbatim-mark rule forbids.
defects.correction: Change the mark to the two strings that are actually printed, carried side by side: "L-2 / L-3 (P401, P402) · L-3 / L-4 (P104)". Rewrite the instanceNote: "P401 and P402 print the PAIR 'L-2 / L-3' on the unit plans; P104 schedules the guestroom lav as L-3 (ADA) / L-4 (non-ADA) and its own L-2 is the EMPLOYEE/POOL wall-hung Decolav Lilac 1819W-1P-CWH with a battery Delta 590TP1150. The drift is the stray L-2 only — L-3 is on both sheets, so the two mark sets overlap rather than conflict outright. 104 is a standard key, so the fixture of record is L-4. Product is HIGH either way: L-3 and L-4 schedule the identical Decolav Callensia 1402-CWH with the identical Delta 581LF-GPM-PP trim, so the mark question is a paperwork risk on the PO, not a wrong-bowl risk in the room." That last point matters — it downgrades the money risk on this line from "wrong lavatory arrives" to nearly nil, because L-3 and L-4 are the same product.

P402.md line 22: "WC-3 / WC-4 (water closet), L-2 / L-3 (lavatory), SH-1 (shower)…". defects.line: Fire Protection — "⊗ SCWLED (kn 43)", qty 3, and Low Voltage — "DB (kn 28)" doorbell; both instanceNotes on the floor-1 hearing-impaired key
defects.problem: Both lines frame the question as A100 vs G001 with A100 favoured ("A100's HI column validates well"), and both declare 104 a live candidate on that basis. They never mention E103 — which is a third in-set source, carries the HI breakdown by room type, and sides with G001. E103's TYPICAL GUEST ROOMS LOAD ANALYSIS prints "King Studio, HI, CD" and "King Studio, HI" as two SEPARATE rows, 1 and 6, exactly matching G001's split; A100 carries an undivided "King Studio, HI = 7" with no CD row. The building total agrees at 7 either way, so the only thing in dispute is whether the floor-1 HI King Studio is the CONNECTING one. If G001 and E103 are right it is 116, and 104 is not a candidate at all — which removes the entire basis for the qty-3 strobe line and the doorbell line. Omitting a corroborating source that flips the conclusion, on the line the list itself calls "THE HIGHEST-VALUE UNKNOWN ON THE 104 SHEET", is the wrong way round. This is aggravated by the fact that E103 is cited five times elsewhere in this same list, for VA loads.
defects.correction: Add to both instanceNotes: "THIRD SOURCE, AND IT SIDES WITH G001. E103's guestroom load analysis carries 'King Studio, HI, CD' (1 room) and 'King Studio, HI' (6 rooms) as separate type rows — the same 1+6 split G001 prints, against A100's undivided 7. Building totals agree at 7; the dispute is only whether the floor-1 HI King Studio is the CONNECTING one. Two of three in-set sources say it is, which points at 116, not at one of the six plain King Studios. That LOWERS the probability that 104 is the communication-features key, and it is a lead not a closure — A100's floor-1 plan still has never been scanned for the E500 crossed-ear symbol. Note also that G001's own HI rows sum to 10 against its printed 'Required 12 / Provided 12' (conflicts.md A11), so G001 is not clean either." Keep both lines at qty-if-applicable and keep the pre-walk action, but add E103 and G001's floor-1 column to the sources to be read.
defects.citation: E103 TYPICAL GUEST ROOMS LOAD ANALYSIS, rows 2 and 6: "King Studio, HI, CD | 387 | … | A | 1" and "King Studio, HI | 387 | … | A | 6". G001 matrix: "King Studio, HI, CD … 1" and "King Studio, HI … 2 | 2 | 2 = 6". Against A100 GUESTROOM MATRIX: "King Studio, HI | – | 1 T | 2 S | 2 S | 2 S | 7" with no HI,CD row at all. G001 flag: "Hearing-impaired arithmetic does not foot. The HI rows sum to 10 … but both tables state 12 required / 12 provided."

defects.line: Mechanical — EF-1, "Toilet exhaust fan — M201 schedules Panasonic FV-0511VK2…" (and by extension the bath switch line kn3)
defects.problem: The line correctly frames the fan-vs-grille conflict (C-06) but misses a second, independent conflict sitting on top of it, and it is one that decides whether the walker writes something up. M201's EF-1 remark 3 reads "switch w/ room lights" — the fan shares the light switch. G402 general note 3 reads, verbatim, "CEILING MOUNTED LIGHT FIXTURE AND FAN TO BE SWITCHED SEPARATELY FROM LIGHT." Those cannot both be satisfied. The verifyAtPunch as written says "confirm which switch controls it" without telling the walker that a fan wired to the bath light is compliant under M201 and non-compliant under G402, so whichever they find, they cannot tell whether it is a defect. Compounding it, the list cites G402 GN3 on the WRONG line — it appears on the entry/kitchenette/closet lighting line, where there is no fan in the room at all.
defects.correction: Move the G402 GN3 citation off the entry/closet lighting line and onto the EF-1 line, and add to the EF-1 instanceNote: "SECOND CONFLICT ON THE SAME DEVICE, AND IT DECIDES A WRITE-UP. M201 EF-1 remark 3 = 'switch w/ room lights' (shared switch). G402 general note 3, verbatim: 'CEILING MOUNTED LIGHT FIXTURE AND FAN TO BE SWITCHED SEPARATELY FROM LIGHT.' Mutually exclusive. If a fan is found and it is on the bath light switch, that is compliant with M201 and non-compliant with G402 — RECORD the wiring, do NOT write it up, and roll it into the same C-06 RFI." verifyAtPunch: "…if a fan: operate it, record WHICH switch controls it and whether the fan and light are on the same switch or separate switches, and confirm the backdraft damper is audible."
defects.citation: M201 Exhaust Fan Schedule, EF-1 remarks "1,2,3,5,6,9" with remark code "3 = switch w/ room lights". G402 general note 3, verbatim: "CEILING MOUNTED LIGHT FIXTURE AND FAN TO BE SWITCHED SEPARATELY FROM LIGHT".

defects.line: Electrical — S21 bath downlight (src "E101 · E400 · E201") and entry/kitchenette/closet lighting (src "E400 … · E201 ('entry/closet lights')")
defects.problem: E201 is the SECOND FLOOR plan. Room 104 is on the first floor. The first-floor lighting sheet is E200, and E200 explicitly does NOT show guestroom lighting — its guestroom wing is shaded with two callouts "Refer to Enlarged Guestroom Plan (E-400)." So the only floor-plan support these two lines actually have for 104 is E400, and the entry/closet line's second pillar ("E201 names it") evaporates entirely for this room. It does not change the conclusion — E400 independently lists "entry/closet/general lights" — but a first-floor punch sheet citing a second-floor plan is the kind of thing that gets a whole package's citations distrusted, and it will be repeated across all 16 first-floor rooms.
defects.correction: Strike E201 from both src strings. On the S21 line: src becomes "E101 Lighting Fixture Schedule row S21 · E400 (King Studio detail 01)". On the entry/closet line: src becomes "E400 (fixtures present, untyped; 'entry/closet/general lights' named in E400's per-room lighting) · E200 (first-floor lighting plan — guestroom wing shaded, refers to E-400, so no floor-plan source exists for floor 1) · E101 Lighting Fixture Schedule has NO guestroom general/entry/closet row". Add to the entry/closet instanceNote: "Note there is no first-floor lighting plan support at all — E200 defers the whole guestroom wing to E400 — so E400's PDF is the only place a count or a type tag can come from."
defects.citation: E101 Electrical Drawings index: "E200 Lighting First Floor Plan; E201 Lighting & Power Second Floor Plan". E200 View and content: "West ~half — GUESTROOM wing: shaded; lighting not shown here — two callouts 'Refer to Enlarged Guestroom Plan (E-400).'" E201 View and content: "Whole second-floor combined lighting + power plan."

defects.line: Electrical — entry/kitchenette/closet lighting, where: "A555 view 04 prints 'CENTER OVER CLOSET' on the companion sheet"
defects.problem: A555 is the Queen-Queen sheet — "ENL. GUEST ROOM PLANS & ELEVS - QQ STD., QQ EXT., & QQ STD. CONN." Room 104 is a King Studio, governed by A550. The King Studio and the Queen-Queen have different plans, different entry-leg geometry and different closet positions, so a location note lifted off A555 is not a location for 104. The line calls it "the companion sheet," which softens it, but it sits in the `where` field where a walker reads it as the answer. The same wrong-type reliance appears on the WAG-30 line ("on A555 the same keynote lands on the bed-wall/sofa-wall elevation"), though there it is disclosed more honestly as a cross-type observation.
defects.correction: Move it out of `where` and into the instanceNote, marked as cross-type: "A555 (the QUEEN-QUEEN sheet, not the King Studio sheet) prints 'CENTER OVER CLOSET' at its entry closet. A550 — the sheet that governs 104 — carries no equivalent printed note and no general-lighting keynote on its view-02 RCP, so the closet fixture's position in a King Studio is not stated anywhere. Cross-type read, offered as a lead only." `where` becomes: "Entry / kitchenette leg (7'-3" ceiling per A550 view 02) and the closet — exact positions not stated on A550."
defects.citation: A555 title block: "A555 — ENL. GUEST ROOM PLANS & ELEVS - QQ STD., QQ EXT., & QQ STD. CONN." and A555 line 109: "Printed note 'CENTER OVER CLOSET' at the entry closet." A550 title block: "ENL. GUEST ROOM PLANS & ELEVS - KING STD. & KING STD. CONN."; A550 view 02 RCP keynotes are 31, 18, 19, 4, 1, 8 — no general-lighting note.

defects.line: Plumbing — GV, gate valves, instanceNote: "P101 note 9 requires the GC to furnish access panels"
defects.problem: Scope reversed. P101 note 9 reads "Furnish access panels (installed by GC) as required" — i.e. the note sits in the PLUMBING general notes and directs the plumbing contractor to FURNISH, with the GC INSTALLING. The line has it backwards, which puts the buy on the wrong party. On a line whose whole point is "if there is NO panel anywhere, write that up against P101 note 15," getting who owes the panel backwards is the difference between a chargeable back-charge and an own-cost fix.
defects.correction: Change to: "P101 note 9 verbatim: 'Furnish access panels (installed by GC) as required' — the PLUMBING contractor (Larry's) furnishes the panel, the GC installs it. Name both before the walk or it becomes nobody's, the same way M401 records the PTAC-condensate seam." Keep P101 note 15 and M101 N7 as cited — both check out.

P101 note 15, verbatim: "Valves (domestic water): ball valves or approved equal, located accessibly." M101 N7: "Access panels in ceilings/walls to valves, traps, dampers, cleanouts, controls — min 12"×12".

defects.line: Mechanical — PTAC wall sleeve kit, verifyAtPunch: "…no air whistle; measure clear to bottom of sleeve, min 3-1/4" AFF; sleeve pitched to drain OUT."
defects.problem: "Sleeve pitched to drain OUT" is not on any sheet. M501 detail 9 says the sleeve is furnished with the unit, caulked all around, sealed per manufacturer, min 3-1/4" AFF, with a drain kit and condensate run down the wall — it states no pitch. It is a true fact about PTAC sleeves generally and a false statement about this drawing set, and it is a criterion a walker could reject an otherwise-conforming installation on. Under the never-invent rule it has to go or be labelled.
defects.correction: Either delete the clause, or rewrite it as: "…min 3-1/4" AFF. NOTE: no sheet in this set specifies sleeve pitch — if the sleeve reads flat or pitched in, record it against the G.E. installation instructions in the approved submittal rather than writing it up against a drawing." Same treatment for the card-lock line's "closer self-latches the door from 30° open" — A600 Set #1 lists only "1 Door Closer w/ 90° Stop", so 30° is an NFPA 80 test convention, not a sheet requirement.
defects.citation: M501 detail 9, PACKAGED TERMINAL A/C UNIT: "wall sleeve furnished with unit, caulked all around; aluminum architectural-style grille factory-painted to match exterior wall; seal sleeves/penetrations per manufacturer; drain kit for 1st/2nd/3rd/4th-floor units (furnished with unit); field-built sub-base (see arch); run condensate drain down wall (see plumbing for continuation); min 3-1/4" AFF; air filter + return-air path shown." No pitch stated. A600 Door Hardware Set #1: "1 Door Closer w/ 90° Stop".

defects.line: Mechanical — PTAC drain kit, label: "(furnished with the unit; M501 det.9 calls it out for 1st-floor units)"
defects.problem: M501 detail 9 calls the drain kit out for "1st/2nd/3rd/4th-floor units" — that is, every floor. Writing it as a first-floor callout implies a floor-1-specific requirement the detail does not make, and a reader building the other three floors' packages off this wording would conclude the drain kit is not required above floor 1. It is a small misquote on an otherwise-correct HIGH line, but it is exactly the kind that propagates at 115 keys.
defects.correction: Label becomes: "PTAC drain kit (furnished with the unit; M501 det.9 calls it out for 1st/2nd/3rd/4th-floor units — i.e. all floors)".
defects.citation: M501 detail 9, verbatim: "drain kit for 1st/2nd/3rd/4th-floor units (furnished with unit)".

defects.line: Fire Protection — all three sprinkler head lines, label: "Sprinkler head on drop — Viking VK430, K=4.3, 1/2" thread (FP-1 description column verbatim)"
defects.problem: Two small breaches of the verbatim rule on lines that otherwise handle the concealed/semi-recessed conflict well. (1) "Viking" is not printed anywhere on FP-1's head schedule — the schedule's columns are Symbol / Count 1st flr / Count all flrs / Thread / K-Factor / Description / Note, and the Description column prints only "VK430 7/16 FR 155 C PD". VK is Viking's prefix and the inference is almost certainly right, but the list correctly refuses to decode "C" or "155" on the same row and then decodes "VK" without saying so. (2) The parenthetical "(FP-1 description column verbatim)" sits after "1/2" thread", but 1/2" comes from the separate Thread column and K=4.3 from the K-Factor column — only the model string is from Description. Third, trivial: head 1's `where` reads "Bed / window area", which is the wording from room 107 (Queen-Queen); the room-108 King Studio reading says "bed area".
defects.correction: Label becomes: "Sprinkler head on drop — FP-1 description column verbatim 'VK430 7/16 FR 155 C PD'; Thread column 1/2", K-Factor column 4.3; head 1 of 3". Add to the instanceNote: "FP-1 prints no MANUFACTURER column — 'Viking' is a decode of the VK prefix, not a printed word, and must not go on a purchase document off this row any more than a temperature rating or a finish may." Change head 1's `where` to "Bed area" to match the room-108 reading actually relied on.
defects.citation: packages/fire-appliance.md §1.1, FP-1 Sprinkler Head Schedule columns: "Symbol | Count 1st flr | Count all flrs | Thread | K-Factor | Description (verbatim) | Note" — row: "◉ | 62 | 437 | 1/2" | 4.3 | VK430 7/16 FR 155 C PD | ON DROP". §1.3, room 108: "1. bed area — 1¼" @ 12-8, 'Drop 0-3'"; room 107: "1. bed / window area".

defects.line: Plumbing — TP, "Trap guard / trap primer…", instanceNote: "TWO DIFFERENT TRAP-PRIMER PRODUCTS ARE SCHEDULED"
defects.problem: There are three named devices in play, not two, and the one the line omits is the one that matches its own label and its own verify step. P104's Drain and Drainage Appurtenance Schedule names a trap-guard mark, TG-1, on three rows — FD-1, FD-2 and FS, each "w/ trap guard TG-1" — but TG-1 has NO schedule row of its own anywhere in P104, so it has no manufacturer and no model. That is a cleaner statement of the gap than the two-primer framing: the verify step tells the walker to "look for a trap guard fitted in the drain body," and the set names that guard TG-1 and then never specifies it.
defects.correction: Rewrite the first sentence: "THREE DEVICES ARE NAMED AND NONE IS SCOPED TO A GUESTROOM. (a) P102 schedules the Automatic Trap Primer Valve as Sioux Chief 695 Series, 30–250 PSIG, 'installed in accessible locations per notes (NPCA/ASSE 1018)'. (b) P104 schedules TP-1 = PPP SMP-500-115V and scopes it to a 6" SUMP PUMP STANDPIPE. (c) P104 names a trap-guard mark TG-1 on FD-1, FD-2 and FS — but TG-1 has NO row of its own in the schedule, so the trap GUARD, which is what the verify step actually looks for, has no manufacturer or model anywhere in the set. Meanwhile P301 general note 6 requires a guard or primer at EVERY floor drain." SETTLES IT stays the same.
defects.citation: P104 Drain and Drainage Appurtenance Schedule: "FD-1 | Floor Drain (Mechanical, Laundry Room) | Zurn | Z550 | w/ trap guard TG-1"; "FD-2 | … | Zurn | Z415B | w/ trap guard TG-1"; "FS | Floor Sink | Zurn | Z1996-2 | w/ trap guard TG-1" — no TG-1 row exists. P104 summary: "trap guards (TG-1) on FD-1/FD-2/FS. Only one trap primer (TP-1) is active." P102 §5: "TP — Sioux Chief 695 Series, 30–250 PSIG, single trap." P301 note 6: "All floor drains to be installed with trap guards / primers."

defects.line: Electrical — mark "PNL \"A\""; and Mechanical — PTAC-1 src "A550 KN1 / KN30 / view 08"
defects.problem: Two citation-hygiene slips against the verbatim rule the list otherwise enforces well. (1) E400 prints the schedule header as PANEL "A" (TYPICAL); "PNL" is E101's abbreviation-legend shorthand ("PNL = panel"), so "PNL \"A\"" is a normalised mark, not a printed one — the same class of tidying the list rightly refuses on "PTAC-2 / PTAC-1" and "SH-1 / SH-4". (2) The PTAC src groups KN30 with view 08, but A550 keynote 30 ("EDGE OF PTAC ABOVE CARPET TILES") is placed on view 03, the FINISH plan; view 08 carries keynotes 1 and 4 only. The KN30 requirement is real and correctly used in verifyAtPunch — only the view attribution is wrong.
defects.correction: Mark becomes PANEL "A". PTAC src becomes "M201 PTAC schedule · M401 KN3 + detail 03 (King Std.) · M301 first-floor plan · M501 det.9 · A550 KN1 (views 01 and 08) / KN30 (view 03, finish plan) / view 08 window-wall elevation".
defects.citation: E400: "PANEL \"A\" (TYPICAL) — standard guestroom. Location: Bedroom; 120/208V, 1-phase, 3-wire, NEMA 1; MCB 100A." E101 abbreviations: "PNL = panel". A550 view 03 Finish plan: "Keynote 13 …, 22 …, 30 (edge of PTAC above carpet tiles), 5, 4"; A550 view 08: "keynotes 1 (PTAC) and 4 (shade)".

defects.line: Electrical — WS03, S21, kn18 lines (and the sconce lines if added): no line applies E400 General Note 7
defects.problem: E400's guestroom general notes include a mounting-envelope rule that applies to every wall-mounted fixture and device in the room and is not scoped to accessible keys: "Wall-mount fixtures/devices 27"–80" AFF; protrude ≤ 4" from wall per accessibility." It is repeated on A530 general note H and again in G400/G402 schedule general note 3. Nothing on this list uses it. It is the one accessibility criterion on the sheet that is not caught in the open 12"/18"/46"/48"/54" height fight, so it is actually enforceable at punch today — a vanity sconce or a nightstand sconce projecting more than 4" in the circulation path is a defect the walker can call with confidence.
defects.correction: Add to the verifyAtPunch of WS03 and any sconce lines added: "measure the projection from the wall face — must not exceed 4" for anything mounted between 27" and 80" AFF (E400 GN7 / A530 GN H / G400-G402 schedule GN3); this one IS enforceable, unlike the open mounting-height conflict."
defects.citation: E400 General Notes (typical guestroom) note 7: "Wall-mount fixtures/devices 27"–80" AFF; protrude ≤ 4" from wall per accessibility." A530 GENERAL NOTES - GUESTROOMS note H: "OBJECTS MOUNTED W/IN THE CIRCULATION PATH … B/T 27" & 80" A.F.F. SHALL NOT PROTRUDE FARTHER THAN 4" FROM WALL."
